Format numbers and p-values for figures and tables

Source: R/fmt.R
fmt_sci.Rd

  • fmt_sci() writes numbers in scientific notation with a multiplication sign and Unicode superscript exponents (2.1 x 10 to the power -6 is printed with a raised -6), readable in gt tables, DT tables, ggplot2 texts and inline text without LaTeX.

  • fmt_num() uses fixed decimals, and switches to scientific notation when the value would print as 0 (|x| < 0.5 x 10^-digits) or is very large (|x| >= 1e6).

  • fmt_p() formats p-values: "0.023", "0.0024", and scientific notation below sci_below; values under the machine precision are written as "< 2.2 x 10 to the power -16".

  • fmt_stars() converts p-values into significance stars.

Usage

fmt_sci(x, digits = 2)

fmt_num(x, digits = 2, sci_digits = 2)

fmt_p(p, digits = 2, sci_below = 0.001)

fmt_stars(p, ns = "ns", trend = TRUE)

Arguments

x, p

Numeric vector (NA allowed).

digits

Significant digits of the mantissa (fmt_sci(), fmt_p()) or number of decimals (fmt_num()).

sci_digits

Significant digits used when fmt_num() switches to scientific notation.

sci_below

p-values below this threshold are written in scientific notation.

ns

Symbol of a non-significant p-value.

trend

If TRUE, "." marks 0.05 <= p < 0.10.

Value

A character vector of the same length as the input ("NA" for missing values, "" in fmt_stars()).

Examples

fmt_sci(c(0.000021, 123456789))
#> [1] "2.1×10⁻⁵" "1.2×10⁸" 
fmt_num(c(1.23456, 0.0001, NA), digits = 2)
#> [1] "1.23"     "1.0×10⁻⁴" "NA"      
fmt_p(c(0.2, 0.0312, 0.00012, 1e-20))
#> [1] "0.2"        "0.031"      "1.2×10⁻⁴"   "<2.2×10⁻¹⁶"
fmt_stars(c(0.2, 0.07, 0.03, 0.004, 0.0001))
#> [1] "ns"  "."   "*"   "**"  "***"
